title: What Is Next.js?
summary: Next.js is a framework that adds routing and server features around React.

subtopics.title: React connection
subtopics.explanation: React components describe interface pieces; Next.js uses them while adding conventions for a complete application. For example, a product card can be rendered inside a Next.js page. Learning components, props, and state first makes framework behavior easier to understand. React remains the component model, while the framework supplies conventions around the app. Understanding that distinction helps locate whether a behavior comes from React or Next.js. React components are like building blocks; Next.js adds the plan for the whole building.

subtopics.title: Routes
subtopics.explanation: A route is an address that displays a page. Next.js can create routes from folders and special files. A folder such as `about` can map to an address people open directly. Test the address after refresh, not only after navigating from the home page. File conventions create routes, but the server must still return the intended page for direct requests. Keep route URLs stable when possible because people bookmark and share them. A route is like a street address that leads to one page.

subtopics.title: Server and browser
subtopics.explanation: Some code runs on the server before a response is sent; other code runs in the browser for interaction. Keep credentials on the server. A browser component can handle a menu click, while server code can load private data without bundling its credentials. Server and browser code have different access to secrets, APIs, and interactive state. Keep credentials in server-only paths and send only the data needed by the interface. Server code is like a workshop preparing a package; browser code is the part a visitor uses.

subtopics.title: Rendering choices
subtopics.explanation: A page can be generated ahead of a request, created for each request, or updated over time. Match the choice to freshness and personalization. A public article may be prepared ahead; a private dashboard may need user-specific data. Consider caching and server work as part of the choice. Render and cache choices affect freshness, privacy, and cost. A public article and a personalized dashboard should not automatically share the same data strategy. Pre-rendering is like preparing a public menu ahead; request rendering is like making a meal for one guest.

subtopics.title: Project conventions
subtopics.explanation: Next.js gives special meaning to file names and locations, connecting pages and layouts. A layout can hold shared navigation while a page holds route-specific content. Check the documentation for the version installed in the project because conventions and features evolve. Framework conventions change between versions. Check the project’s installed version and official documentation before copying configuration from an older example. Framework file names are like labeled slots in a kit that tell each part where to go.

foundations.overview: Next.js is a framework for building web applications with React. It adds conventions for routes, server and browser code, rendering, and deployment. Think of React as the pieces used to build the rooms and Next.js as the plan for the whole building. The framework provides choices and defaults; developers still decide how data, accessibility, security, and performance should work.
foundations.whyItMatters: Next.js adds application conventions around React, including routing and server rendering. Distinguishing framework behavior from React behavior helps locate bugs and make sound rendering decisions.
commonUseCases: Build a multi-route React application with shared layout.
Render public pages efficiently while keeping private work on the server.
Deploy an app using framework conventions for pages and assets.
Build a multi-route React application with shared layouts.
Render public content efficiently while keeping private work on the server.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Next.js is a replacement for learning React.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Next.js builds on React, so component, state, and props fundamentals still matter.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Every page must run entirely on the server.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Interactive behavior may use browser components, while server-rendered parts can prepare data and markup.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A framework automatically chooses the best rendering strategy.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Developers still need to match rendering and caching to freshness, privacy, and personalization needs.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Next.js means developers no longer need React fundamentals.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Components, props, state, and events remain the base for building its interfaces.

visualExplorer.title: What Next.js adds to React
visualExplorer.caption: Step through the layers Next.js stacks on top of plain React.

config.intro: Start with bare React and watch each capability Next.js layers on.

steps.name: React core
steps.detail: You have a component-based UI library — it renders the view but provides no routing, server rendering, or backend.

steps.name: File-based routing
steps.detail: Next maps your app/ folder structure to URLs, so files become routes with no router config.

steps.name: Rendering strategies
steps.detail: Each route can be SSR, SSG, ISR, or CSR — server-rendered, static, periodically regenerated, or client-rendered.

steps.name: Full-stack layer
steps.detail: Route Handlers, Server Components, and Server Actions let backend code live alongside the UI.

steps.name: Built-in optimizations
steps.detail: Automatic code splitting plus next/image and next/font give performance wins with zero setup.

steps.name: Deploy
steps.detail: Ship to Vercel with one command or self-host on any Node.js environment.

interactiveExamples.explanation: Next.js renders ordinary React components. This is a plain component just like one you'd put in a Next.js page — the framework adds routing and rendering around it.
interactiveExamples.expectedOutput: A heading, a counter, and a button that increments the count.

interactiveExamples.title: How files map to routes (illustrative)
interactiveExamples.explanation: This illustrative demo renders the file-to-URL mapping Next.js uses. In a real Next.js project these files live on disk; the framework reads the folder tree and creates the routes automatically.

codeLab.title: Match the need to what Next.js provides
codeLab.instructions: For each requirement, fill in which Next.js feature solves it. Edit the component to print your answers, then Run. (Good SEO; an API endpoint; optimized images; a /pricing page.)
codeLab.expectedOutput: Your chosen Next.js feature for each requirement.
hints: Each requirement maps to one headline Next.js capability.
Think: rendering for SEO, route handlers for APIs, next/image for images, file routing for URLs.

keyTakeaways: React components describe interface pieces; Next.
A route is an address that displays a page.
Some code runs on the server before a response is sent; other code runs in the browser for interaction.
